A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and can be matched across the formatting and numbering changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic regression experiments comparing ICL with principled estimators, plus experiments varying model size and training context length.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments examining excess-risk behavior in Mamba and LSTM.

M1.justification: The transformer learning procedure, squared-error objective, analytic predictors, and benchmarking framework remain unchanged. Mamba and LSTM are additional experimental comparisons, rather than a revised proposed learning method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same hierarchical Fourier regression task and noise/weight-variance scenarios. The new architecture experiments reuse the existing scenario with M=10, noise variance 0.03, and weight variance 10; they introduce no new task or domain.

E2.justification: Appendix A.4 adds Mamba and LSTM as alternative sequence-model comparisons for excess-risk behavior. The original comparisons involving BMA, AIC, BIC, BMC, and the equal-weight ensemble are retained.

E3.justification: Section 2.1 changes the reported target-function normalization from sqrt(2m+1) to sqrt(m+1); the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun or documentation was corrected. New Figure A1 evaluates Mamba and LSTM with training prompt lengths of 100, 200, and 400. Existing main-experiment settings and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.4 tests whether non-vanishing excess risk is specific to transformers, using Mamba and LSTM under one retained regression scenario. The existing model-size, context-length, and convergence analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 adds a checklist explanation that most figures omit error bars because they summarize 512 experiments. It also introduces an inconsistency: the checklist calls Figure 1's shading standard error, while its retained caption says standard deviation. No increase in repetitions or new statistical procedure is established.

E6.justification: New Figure A1 reports non-vanishing excess-risk curves for Mamba and LSTM across three training lengths. The original plots and numerical findings are retained, including the mean performance ratio of approximately 1.45 at performance quantile 0.99. The transformer scaling results are relocated, not newly obtained results.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 revises the mathematical target-function normalization and corrects the identity-matrix rank from 2m-1 to 2m+1. The central excess-risk assumption, Theorems 4.2–4.3, and their Appendix B proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions and claims remain: a sample-complexity benchmarking framework, near-optimal few-shot efficiency followed by diminishing many-shot efficiency, and an information-theoretic explanation. The expanded abstract makes the existing regression setting more explicit.

C2.justification: v2 clarifies population-level BMA optimality versus optimality under an empirical pretraining distribution, discusses possible sources of non-vanishing excess risk, and explicitly identifies small model size and limited training-data diversity as applicability limitations. Appendix A.4 extends the architectural interpretation using the new results.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code access link and reports RTX 8000 and A100 hardware in Appendix A.2. The transformer configuration, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and training iterations were already disclosed in v1. Detailed Mamba/LSTM configurations remain sparse.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds recent work on simpler-hypothesis preferences, causal-structure inference, and implicit MLP updates, while removing the dedicated Scaling ICL discussion and some associated references. New appendix citations support the architecture experiments and modern-LLM limitations; the central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are revised, several explanations are expanded, and the redundant Section 2.5 is removed while Appendix A.1 remains. Acknowledgments and a conference checklist are added. The main argumentative sequence and appendix organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main text from two columns to a single-column layout, combines v1 Figures 3 and 4 into Figure 3(a–b), moves the original Figure A1 to main-text Figure 4, and adds a new architecture Figure A1. Appendix figures are also resized and redistributed.

improvement.justification: The Mamba/LSTM experiments provide limited additional support for generality beyond transformers, while clearer limitations and new code-access and hardware information improve transparency. These gains are tempered by sparse implementation details for the new architectures and the introduced Figure 1 standard-error/standard-deviation inconsistency. The central results and proofs are otherwise retained.
